observed_events.description: Landslide at Dzudza on NH-29 between Kohima and Dimapur. An official order closed a short stretch for landslide removal, and the Kohima Deputy Commissioner later reported complete blockage and advised light vehicles to use alternate routes. A fresh mudslide after heavy rain on 22 August hindered restoration.
observed_events.date_note: Sources differ: closure order for removal work covers 16-18 Aug 2024; a PTI report published 20 Aug 2024 places a blockage on Monday 19 Aug; a regional report mentions a fresh mudslide on 22 Aug.
observed_events.location_text: NH-29 near Dzudza bridge, Sechu Zubza; chainage km 163+980 to 164+030 per the Kohima district advisory

observed_events.description: Landslide on the night of 22 August cut the Kohima-Khonoma road, one of the alternate routes advised while NH-29 was blocked at Dzudza.
A portion of NH-29 on the Pagla Pahar stretch was washed away by flooding of the Chathe River on the same night as the Pherima landslide, cutting main road connectivity towards Kohima.
observed_events.date_note: Same year inference as the Pherima event. Confirm.
observed_events.location_text: NH-29 Pagla Pahar stretch (Chathe River side)

observed_events.description: Large landslide on the NH-29 stretch near Pherima on the night of 3 September, with loss of life reported, after the highway had reopened to single-lane traffic following the Dzudza blockage.
observed_events.date_note: The articles give 3 September without a year in the retrieved text; 2024 is inferred from later coverage (Sept 2025 'washed away last year') and a Nov 2024 report citing September 2024 landslides. Confirm.
observed_events.location_text: NH-29 near Pherima village, Chumoukedima district

observed_events.description: Repeated monsoon landslides at several vulnerable points on NH-29, with restrictions on heavy vehicles, reported alongside severe damage on NH-2 near Phesama.
observed_events.location_text: NH-29, several points (not individually named in the source)

observed_events.description: A suspension (wire) bridge over the Chathe River linking Chumoukedima and Seithekema was reported swept away or damaged when the river swelled on 14 September. Sources differ on the extent. Not a highway bridge.
observed_events.location_text: Chathe River, between Chumoukedima and Seithekema

observed_events.description: Multiple landslides between Chathe Bridge and New Chumoukedima halted traffic on the Dimapur-Kohima highway on 14 September; the Pagla Pahar stretch reported as washed away again. Police advisories restricted movement and listed alternate routes.
observed_events.location_text: NH-29 between Chathe Bridge and New Chumoukedima (Pagla Pahar)

assumptions: Settlements and hospitals are attached to the nearest road vertex within a distance threshold; access roads below that distance are not modelled. Distances are stored per record (snap_distance_m).
Segments are stretches of road between junctions/attached features; a bridge sits ON every segment that carries it, so closing a bridge is modelled as closing those segments.
Roads are bidirectional unless OSM tags them one-way; reversible/alternating values are treated as bidirectional.
Travel time uses maxspeed tags where present, otherwise placeholder planning speeds per road class (assumed, not measured).
No monsoon_risk labels, failure histories, bed counts or trauma levels are inferred. Observed events are attached to places only when a source names the place.
NEAREST_HOSPITAL is not populated in Phase 1; it needs the routing of Phase 2 and is never authoritative.
